correctness.rationale: The repaired claim is exact strong chromatic index 7. A conflict between distinct duad–syntheme flags is exactly either cross-membership, including when they share an endpoint. The complete 45-entry coloring in repairs/1/RESULT.md passed its self-contained check of all equal-color edge pairs after reconstructing the canonical list; the proof uses the published six-color obstruction. Independently, the fresh standard-library replay /workspace/branches/24c45266-cb6b-47b6-8e5c-b64957ac6274/reproduce_tutte_coxeter.py and its .out.json regenerated the full 30-vertex, 45-edge instance and all induced matchings: (45,720,5160,16920,22680,8520,720,90,10), with maximum size nine. Every size-eight class has a unique parent, two maxima meet in one edge, and no edge lies in three maxima, so with no nine-class at most two eight-classes fit into six, covering at most 44 edges. With a nine-class at most one eight-class fits: two disjoint eights would have to omit their intersections with the nine-class, yet still share their parents' mutual intersection. The sole six-color profile is then (9,8,7,7,7,7). Each of the 90 ordered parent pairs leaves 32 candidate sevens, and fresh exhaustive tests found no cover by four. The frozen mathematical assertions therefore also check out; the repair addresses coverage, not a false enumeration. Frozen scripts and recorded outputs were inspected, not run. No conclusion for a larger family or list-coloring follows.

evidence: For the balanced partition {A,B}, its maximum matching uses each crossing duad with the syntheme containing it and the remaining internal pair of each side. For a fixed flag (D,S), place the endpoints of D on opposite sides and attach the other two pairs of S, one to each side. There are exactly two partitions. Conversely, two distinct balanced partitions have intersections of sizes 1,2,2,1 after a choice of order. The two singleton intersections together specify D, and the two size-two intersections specify the other pairs in S. This specifies their unique common flag.

evidence: The cubic Tutte eight-cage is the same duad–syntheme graph. Coloring its squared line graph is coloring its edge-conflict graph, or partitioning its compatibility graph into cliques.
The paper names the same cage and says it has no strong six-edge-coloring, not that the chromatic number of its squared line graph is 7.

value.rationale: The repaired result computes a natural invariant of the canonical cubic girth-eight cage, singled out as a six-color obstruction in the literature. An explicit seven-coloring resolves the exact value needed to compare that obstruction with the broader seven-color conjecture. This is useful without claiming a general upper bound or counting the already-covered matching design as new value.
